snippets.output: The patient has hemodynamic instability with blood pressure 92/52 mmHg, pulse 145/min, respirations 33/min, and oxygen saturation 90%. The initial management, including intubation and blood transfusions, is consistent with trauma protocols and addresses immediate life-threatening conditions.
On physical examination, the patient has a rash at the corners of his mouth (angular cheilitis), sparse hair falling out, multiple loose bowel movements, and poor wound healing observed on day 6.
Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency can cause angular cheilitis and stomatitis but is less likely to cause poor wound healing and hair loss.
Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency is related to conditions like beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, which do not correspond with the described symptoms.
Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) can lead to poor wound healing, easy bruising, and bleeding gums, but is less likely to cause hair loss and diarrhea.
Vitamin D deficiency mainly leads to bone-related issues such as osteomalacia and rickets, not specifically the symptoms described here.
Zinc deficiency can cause alopecia (hair loss), dermatitis (rashes), diarrhea, and poor wound healing, aligning well with the patient's symptoms. The most likely deficiency is Zinc.
